# postcaptcha: replace a CAPTCHA with a Polyguard Trust Check

Instructions for a coding agent integrating the Polyguard Trust Check widget
into a website form. The widget is a drop-in replacement for reCAPTCHA v2 and
Cloudflare Turnstile. No site key, secret or account is needed to start.

Source and examples: https://github.com/polyguard-ai/trust-check-widget
Human-readable site: https://postcaptcha.com

## What it does

- The page loads one script and places one div inside the form.
- The visitor clicks the box and scans a code with their phone. Polyguard
  checks that a real phone captured the code from the screen (PG-Presence,
  optical distance bounding) and that the phone passed hardware attestation.
- On success the widget adds a hidden input named `pg-trust-check-response`
  to the enclosing form and calls the `data-callback` function.
- The server sends that value to `POST https://api.polyguard.ai/v2/siteverify`
  and checks `success` and `hostname`.

Facts to keep in mind:

- Visitors need a phone. They do not need to install an app.
- A response verifies once and expires 300 seconds after the Trust Check.
  Re-render or reset the widget for a second submission.
- The first Trust Check from a new hostname creates a free account for that
  hostname, limited to 1,000 Trust Checks per ISO week. The site owner can
  claim it later: https://postcaptcha.com/claim
- `localhost`, `127.0.0.1`, `[::1]` and `*.localhost` work, limited to 100
  Trust Checks a day per IP address.
- Every Trust Check is interactive. There is no invisible or score-only mode.

## Step 1: the page

Add the script once per page and the div inside the form:

    <script src="https://cdn.polyguard.ai/sdk/latest/trust-check.js" async defer></script>

    <form method="POST" action="/signup">
      <input name="email" type="email" required>
      <div class="pg-trust-check" data-callback="onVerified" data-action="signup"></div>
      <button id="submit" type="submit" disabled>Create account</button>
    </form>
    <script>
      function onVerified() { document.getElementById('submit').disabled = false; }
    </script>

Supported `data-*` attributes on the div:

- `data-callback`, `data-expired-callback`, `data-error-callback`: names of
  global functions. The error callback receives an error code string.
- `data-action`: up to 32 chars, `[A-Za-z0-9_-]`, echoed by siteverify.
- `data-cdata`: up to 255 chars, echoed by siteverify.
- `data-theme`: `auto` (default), `light`, `dark`.
- `data-size`: `normal` (300x65, default), `compact` (150x140), `flexible`
  (full width, 65 tall).
- `data-execution`: `render` (default) or `execute` (wait for
  `Polyguard.TrustCheck.execute(id)`).
- `data-locale`: `en`, `es`, `ar`, `hi`.
- `data-path`: group pages with dynamic paths (for `/post/12345` set
  `data-path="/post"`).
- `data-scored`: `true` makes a failed presence score fail the check. Default
  `false`.
- `data-response-field-name`: override the hidden input's name.

Existing reCAPTCHA or Turnstile markup also works: the script renders
`.g-recaptcha` and `.cf-turnstile` containers (ignoring `data-sitekey`), keeps
the hidden input named `g-recaptcha-response` or `cf-turnstile-response` for
them, and defines `window.grecaptcha` and `window.turnstile` when the page has
not. The minimum migration is the script URL and the server call.

Explicit JavaScript API, mirroring Turnstile:

    const id = Polyguard.TrustCheck.render('#container', { callback, action: 'signup' });
    Polyguard.TrustCheck.getResponse(id);   // '' until verified
    Polyguard.TrustCheck.reset(id);
    Polyguard.TrustCheck.remove(id);
    Polyguard.TrustCheck.isExpired(id);
    Polyguard.TrustCheck.execute(id);
    Polyguard.TrustCheck.ready(fn);

Load with `trust-check.js?render=explicit&onload=fnName` to render yourself.

## Step 2: the server

    POST https://api.polyguard.ai/v2/siteverify
    Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded   (JSON also accepted)

    response=<pg-trust-check-response>&remoteip=<visitor ip>

Response:

    {
      "success": true,
      "challenge_ts": "2026-10-22T18:40:12Z",
      "hostname": "www.example.com",
      "app_id": "...",
      "link_uuid": "...",
      "link_session_id": "...",
      "action": "signup",
      "cdata": "",
      "score": "PASS",
      "remoteip_matched": true,
      "error-codes": []
    }

Rules:

- Require `success === true` AND `hostname` equal to the hostname your form is
  served from. Without a secret, the hostname comparison is what ties the
  result to your site.
- If you set `data-action`, also compare `action`.
- Use a request timeout (5 seconds is enough) and treat a non-JSON reply as
  a failure.
- `secret` is optional. After the hostname is claimed, the site owner can send
  the App API key as `secret` and require it.
- `remoteip` is optional. It is compared with the address that started the
  Trust Check and reported as `remoteip_matched`; a mismatch does not change
  `success`.
- `error-codes` values: `missing-input-response`, `invalid-input-response`,
  `timeout-or-duplicate`, `invalid-input-secret`, `bad-request`,
  `internal-error`.
- `score` values: `PASS`, `WARN`, `FAIL`, `INCOMPLETE`, `OFFLINE`,
  `NOT_ENABLED`. With `data-scored` off (the default) it is informational.

## Pick the example for the stack

Copy the file that matches, then adapt the hostname constant and the
form-handling code:

- React: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/polyguard-ai/trust-check-widget/main/examples/react/usePolyguardTrustCheck.ts
  and https://raw.githubusercontent.com/polyguard-ai/trust-check-widget/main/examples/react/TrustCheckForm.tsx
- Next.js App Router route handler: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/polyguard-ai/trust-check-widget/main/examples/nextjs/route.ts
- Express middleware: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/polyguard-ai/trust-check-widget/main/examples/express/middleware.js
- Plain HTML: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/polyguard-ai/trust-check-widget/main/examples/html/index.html
- Flask decorator: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/polyguard-ai/trust-check-widget/main/examples/python-flask/verify.py
- PHP: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/polyguard-ai/trust-check-widget/main/examples/php/verify.php
- WordPress notes: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/polyguard-ai/trust-check-widget/main/examples/wordpress/README.md

Any other stack: do Step 1 in the template and Step 2 in the form handler with
the language's HTTP client, following the rules above.

## Migrating from reCAPTCHA v2 or Turnstile

- Script URL: replace with `https://cdn.polyguard.ai/sdk/latest/trust-check.js`.
- Server call: replace the siteverify URL with
  `https://api.polyguard.ai/v2/siteverify`; drop `secret` or keep it empty.
- Optional renames: `class="pg-trust-check"`, field `pg-trust-check-response`,
  `Polyguard.TrustCheck.*` in place of `grecaptcha.*` / `turnstile.*`.
- Not supported: `data-sitekey` (ignored), `data-appearance`, reCAPTCHA
  invisible, Turnstile managed/non-interactive/invisible modes.

Full diffs: https://postcaptcha.com/migrate/recaptcha and
https://postcaptcha.com/migrate/turnstile

## After integrating

Tell the site owner:

- The account for the hostname is free and limited to 1,000 Trust Checks per
  week. To manage it, claim the hostname by publishing
  `/.well-known/polyguard.json`: https://postcaptcha.com/claim
- Visitors need a phone.
